---
title: "Reports and documents"
description: >
  R Markdown and Quarto formats for HTML, Word and PDF reports, slides and
  dashboards, the starter documents, and rendering one document in default
  and accessible colours.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

phwstyle gives whole documents the PHW look: the Ubuntu font, navy
headings, the gradient header band, a cover page for PDFs and slides, and
"Page x of y" footers. You choose a format once in the document's YAML
header, and the charts and tables inside follow the same style.

There are two routes. Use whichever your team already uses:

| | R Markdown (`.Rmd`) | Quarto (`.qmd`) |
|---|---|---|
| Formats | HTML, Word, PDF | HTML, Word, PDF (Typst or LaTeX), slides, dashboards |
| Setup | None: the formats come with phwstyle | Run `use_phw_quarto()` once in each project |
| Charts and flextables | Styled for you | Call `use_phw_ggplot()` and `use_phw_flextable()` in the setup chunk |
| Needs | The rmarkdown package; LaTeX for PDF | Quarto 1.5 or later (recent versions of RStudio include it) |

`phw_setup_check()` tells you whether Pandoc, Quarto and LaTeX are
available on your computer.

## R Markdown

Put a phwstyle format in the YAML header, and knit as usual:

```yaml
---
title: "Report title"
author: "Team name"
output: phwstyle::phw_word_document
---
```

| Format | Output |
|---|---|
| `phwstyle::phw_html_document` | A web page with the header band, a floating table of contents and the PHW Bootstrap theme. Works offline: the fonts are inside the file |
| `phwstyle::phw_word_document` | A Word document built from the PHW reference document: Ubuntu, navy headings, tables with horizontal rules only, a header band and a page footer |
| `phwstyle::phw_pdf_document` | A PDF through LaTeX (XeLaTeX), with a full-page cover, a running header band and a footer |

To start from a working example in RStudio, choose **File > New File > R
Markdown > From Template > PHW report**. It knits to all three formats.

The formats call `use_phw_ggplot()` and `use_phw_flextable()` before
knitting, so don't repeat them in the document. Add `theme_phw()` or a
PHW scale to a plot only to change something for that plot.

Options go under the format name:

```yaml
output:
  phwstyle::phw_pdf_document:
    toc: true
    team: "Team name"
    number_sections: false
```

`?phw_formats` lists every option, including `fig_width` and `fig_height`,
`cover = FALSE` to drop the PDF cover, and `palette`.

## Quarto

Run this once in your project folder. It adds the PHW extension in
`_extensions/phw` and writes a starter report:

```{r}
phwstyle::use_phw_quarto(template = "report")
```

`template = "slides"` and `template = "dashboard"` write a starter
presentation or dashboard instead, and `template = "none"` adds only the
extension. Run it again with `overwrite = TRUE` after updating phwstyle,
to pick up changes to the extension.

Then name the format in the YAML header:

```yaml
---
title: "Report title"
format: phw-docx
---
```

| Format | Output |
|---|---|
| `phw-html` | A web page with the header band and a table of contents |
| `phw-docx` | A Word document built from the PHW reference document |
| `phw-typst` | A PDF through Typst, which comes with Quarto, so no LaTeX is needed. Cover page, running header band, page numbers |
| `phw-pdf` | A PDF through LaTeX, for teams that already use it |
| `phw-revealjs` | 16:9 HTML slides with a title slide, logo and footer |
| `phw-dashboard` | A one-page dashboard with a navy navigation bar and PHW cards |

A Quarto extension styles the page but can't run R code, so style the
charts and tables in the setup chunk, as the starter documents do:

````markdown
```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(phwstyle)
use_phw_ggplot()
use_phw_flextable()
```
````

The Typst PDF takes a few extra options in the YAML header:
`phw-team: "Team name"` adds a team line to the cover, `phw-no-cover:
true` drops the cover, and `phw-org`, `phw-page-label` and `phw-of-label`
change the footer wording. See `?use_phw_quarto`.

To make several formats from one document, list them:

```yaml
format:
  phw-html: default
  phw-docx: default
  phw-typst: default
```

## Default and accessible colours

Some readers need colours that stay distinct for every type of colour
blindness. The `accessible` palette does that, and switching it on for a
document changes every chart, table and widget made with phwstyle (see
[Colours and accessibility](colours.html#colour-blind-safe-colours)).

**To switch a document for good**, add one line to its YAML header. It
works the same in R Markdown and Quarto:

```yaml
phw-palette: accessible
```

**To make both versions from one unchanged document**, set the palette
when you render. In R Markdown, use `output_options`:

```{r}
word <- "phwstyle::phw_word_document"
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report.docx")
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report-accessible.docx",
                  output_options = list(palette = "accessible"))
```

In Quarto, set the environment variable `PHWSTYLE_PALETTE` for the second
render. From R (this works on Windows too):

```{r}
system2("quarto", c("render", "report.qmd", "--to", "phw-docx"))

Sys.setenv(PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible")
system2("quarto", c("render", "report.qmd", "--to", "phw-docx",
                    "-o", "report-accessible.docx"))
Sys.unsetenv("PHWSTYLE_PALETTE")
```

Or from a terminal:

```sh
quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx
PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx -o report-accessible.docx
```

In PowerShell, set it with `$env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible"` before
the second render, and clear it with `Remove-Item Env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE`
afterwards.

The setting has to reach R through the document or the environment:
Quarto doesn't pass `-M` values or `_quarto.yml` settings on to R.

If you keep colour keys in a file (`phw_key_file()` in the setup chunk),
each group keeps its colour in both versions, from one run to the next.

## Fonts and the logo

The fonts travel with the outputs where they can: HTML pages, slides and
dashboards embed Ubuntu, and the PDF formats use the copy inside phwstyle.
Word documents name Ubuntu, so Word shows it only on computers that have
it. Run `phw_install_fonts()` once if you can; otherwise Word uses a
similar font.

The PHW logo isn't included in phwstyle. Without it, every format is
still styled and shows the organisation name instead. To add it, run
`phw_download_logos()` once, or point phwstyle at an approved copy with
`options(phwstyle.logo_dir = "path/to/logos")`. For Quarto, run
`use_phw_quarto(overwrite = TRUE)` afterwards so the extension picks it
up.

## Shiny apps

For an app, `phw_page_navbar()` gives a complete page with the header
band, navigation bar and footer, and `phw_bs_theme()` styles any bslib or
Shiny page:

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
ui <- phw_page_navbar(
  title = "Weekly surveillance",
  nav_panel("Overview", plotOutput("epicurve")),
  nav_panel("Data", reactable::reactableOutput("table"))
)
```

Interactive charts and tables in an app are styled the same way as in an
HTML report: `phw_plotly()`, `phw_reactable()` and `phw_datatable()`.
